newsitem.title: CHINA: China warns Taiwan ships over flags in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China warns Taiwan ships over flags in Hong Kong.

text.p: Taiwanese ships that visit Hong Kong after the British colony returns to Chinese rule next year must not fly any flag that contravenes Beijing's cherished "One China" principle, Chinese officials said on Friday.

Beijing had already decreed that shipping and air links between Hong Kong and Nationalist-ruled Taiwan could continue after the June 30 handover of sovereignty, said an official of the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet.
"When Taiwan-registered ships enter Hong Kong ports, no flag may be flown that creates a "Two Chinas" problem," the official said, but declined to give details.
"I am not authorised to say anything more," he told Reuters by telephone.

Flying the Republic of China flag used by Taipei is banned in China, which has considered Taiwan a rebel province since the defeated Nationalist government fled to the island at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
When vessels registered in Hong Kong visited Taiwan ports they should receive "reciprocal treatment", the State Council official said but declined to elaborate.

Hong Kong has long been a trading conduit between the Chinese mainland and Taiwan, which bans direct shipping links, and Beijing has said it should be able to continue in this role after the end of British colonial rule.

Beijing has repeatedly accused Taipei of wanting to split China by pursuing an informal "Two Chinas" policy. Taiwan's government rejects the charge, saying it still hopes for eventual reunification with the mainland.
